Rina Ortiz: Hi team — I'm landing my first PR to the monorepo (small bugfix in model-serving package). quick sanity check: preferred branching strategy here? and do we squash on merge or keep commits?

Jasper Cole: Welcome! For most feature/fix work we do short-lived branches off main. Branch name format: <type>/<linear>#<num>-short. eg: fix/1234-stale-lock.

Nikhil Rao: We normally ask to squash-and-merge for tiny fixes unless the commit history is meaningful. Put a single tidy commit and a clear message.

Rina Ortiz: Good to know. Our repo is big — anything special about changing protobufs or generated clients?

Jasper Cole: If you change .proto files, also check in the generated Go/Python files in /proto-gen and add a note in PR about regeneration. Ping @infra-proto-review in the PR description.

Rina Ortiz: Got it. Tests: I only changed a util used by runtime. Should I add unit tests in the same package or a separate test-suite?

Nikhil Rao: Same package with a matching test file (test_*.py). Keep tests focused + fast. If it's integration-y, put it behind the test-infra tag so it runs in CI only.

Rina Ortiz: What local checks to run? pre-commit ran but CI still failed for me once with license header error.

Jasper Cole: Run these locally:
```bash
# install dev deps
pip install -r dev-requirements.txt
# run linter + headers
pre-commit run --all-files
# quick unit tests for package
pytest packages/model-serving/tests/test_utils.py -q
```
The license header check is a pre-commit hook (fix with `add_license_header` script in scripts/`).

Rina Ortiz: Thanks. Who should I request for review? small change but touching runtime helpers.

Nikhil Rao: Tag @jasper (package owner) and one backend reviewer. For runtime perf-sensitive changes, also add @grace.

Grace (manager): If it's likely to affect latency, please include a 1-paragraph perf note in the PR and mark it with label:perf-risk. Even small helper changes can bubble up.

Rina Ortiz: Ok will do. Any expectations on PR description length/format?

Jasper Cole: Use the PR template under .github/pull_request_template.md. Short summary + background + testing steps + link to Linear. If you fixed a bug, include reproduction steps.

Rina Ortiz: Merge strategy — do we rebase or merge main before merging?

Nikhil Rao: Rebase onto main is preferred to keep history linear. We use protected branches so you need to pass CI and have at least one approver.

MergeBot: build/1746452100 — checks queued. status: running (unit, lint, mypy) :hourglass:

Rina Ortiz: I saw some PRs get big code-review threads. Any tips to keep it small and reviewable?

Jasper Cole: Split into logical commits and keep PR surface small. If you must change many files, add a summary section with a file list and rationale. Use draft PRs early.

Rina Ortiz: One last: do we squash fixup commits, or use the "squash and merge" button?

Nikhil Rao: Either is fine. If you use the button, make sure the final commit message follows our convention: <type>(scope): short summary — then include a longer body explaining the why.

Rina Ortiz: Thanks everyone! I'll update the PR description with the perf note and regen proto files if needed. Appreciate the quick onboarding help. :tada:

Grace (manager): Welcome aboard again. Ping in this channel if anything blocks you getting green CI.
